The white-haired old man was the {{ill|Kunitama|fr|Kunitama|ja|国魂|simple|Kunitama|zh|國魂|qid=Q9692242|lt=Kunitama deity}}, and this was interpreted as a divine oracle to develop this land. A shrine was built to enshrine this deity, and this is the origin of the shrine. The place name "Shio" (salt) also derives from this event.

During the Meiji era, the shrine was identified as the Shikinaisha Takuhi Reshi Shrine, but "Takuhire" refers to taku cloth (a type of bark cloth), and since this shrine is rather associated with salt, there is also a theory that identifies the Shikinaisha with {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Anekurahime Shrine}} (in Toyama City Kureha-machi) or Gofuku Shrine (in Toyama City Gofuku), which are associated with weaving and clothing.
